layers.why: project tooling, standard library only so it works when the product does not compile
paths of the data directory are a leaf shared by store, workspace, lifecycle and netaccess
process supervision primitives; the only product package that spawns processes
per-employee folders and scrubbed environments are a leaf
single instance, discovery file and autostart are a leaf
bind rules and local token are a leaf
adapters and profiles start processes only through proc and know nothing about the rest of the daemon; its test-support sub-package providertest may import the parent
approvals and audit only need storage
runs employees and sessions; must not know about HTTP
the only contract between daemon and clients; never reaches into providers or processes
Go client for the daemon API, shared by every Go client; knows nothing about daemon internals
performance budgets exercise the whole daemon
small CLI client: talks to the daemon only through internal/client
Wails desktop app (build tag desktop): a client, talks to the daemon only through internal/client

restricted_imports.why: spawning processes is a security boundary: only proc, project tooling and benchmarks may do it
no cgo in our code: the daemon is one static binary that cross-compiles to every platform (the Wails dependency has its own cgo, behind the desktop build tag)
